title: Safe first products: ingredients, hygiene and dilution

say: Safe first products: ingredients, hygiene and dilution.
This is the video for module 1 of Organic Skincare and Hair Products.
This course starts with products that contain no water. Makers call them anhydrous, which means water-free. Germs need water to grow, so oil-only products do not need a preservative against germs.
Their main enemy is rancidity. Oils react with air, light and heat, and start to smell like old groundnuts.
A lotion or cream mixes oil and water. The moment water is present, germs can grow, often without any smell you can notice.
So the rule is simple. If it has water in it, it needs a real preservative and proper training.
You will make four products. Whipped shea butter, for dry skin and for sealing moisture into natural hair.

say: Every product is built from three families. Butters give body. Shea butter is soft and rich, and melts close to skin temperature. Cocoa butter is much harder.

cards.d: Shea is soft and rich and melts near skin temperature. Cocoa butter is harder.
Light oils sink in. Heavy oils like castor coat and shine. Blend them.
Beeswax turns oils into a balm. More wax makes it harder.

say: Liquid oils give spread and softness. A light oil sinks in quickly. A heavy oil like castor is thick and sticky, so use it as a smaller part of a blend.

cards.d: Shea is soft and rich and melts near skin temperature. Cocoa butter is harder.

Beeswax turns oils into a balm. More wax makes it harder.

say: Wax gives structure. Beeswax melts at roughly 62 to 64 degrees Celsius, so balms stay firm in the heat.
Oils soften and protect hair, but do not promise that any oil makes hair grow.

say: Clean work separates a professional from a hobbyist. Clear the table of food, pets and children, and tie back your hair.

panel.heading: Clean routine before every batch
items: Clear the table of food, pets and children
Wash the surface, wipe with 70% alcohol
Wash tools in hot soapy water, dry fully
Sanitise tools and jars, let them air-dry
Gloves on; tools kept for products only

say: Wash the table, then wipe it with 70% alcohol and let it dry.

say: Essential oils are very concentrated plant extracts. Used too strong, they can burn or sensitise skin. Always dilute them in a carrier oil.

panel.heading: Safe essential oil dilution
items: Sensitive or damaged skin: 0.2 to 1%
Face products: 0.5 to 1.2%
Body oils and butters: 1 to 3%
Scalp oils in this course: 1% or below
Baby products: leave essential oils out

say: For sensitive or damaged skin, 0.2 to 1%.

say: Some oils need extra care. Tea tree, peppermint, cinnamon and clove are known skin irritants. Keep them low, and keep peppermint and eucalyptus away from the faces of babies and small children.

cards.d: Tea tree, peppermint, cinnamon, clove: never undiluted, keep levels low.
Cold-pressed lemon, lime and bergamot can cause burns on sunny skin.
Store out of children's reach. A child drinking a bottle: hospital at once, with the bottle.

say: Cold-pressed citrus oils, like lemon, lime and bergamot, can cause burns on skin in the sun. Choose steam-distilled versions or other oils.

say: And never let anyone swallow essential oils. A small child drinking a bottle is a medical emergency. Go to a hospital immediately, with the bottle.

say: To remember. Start with water-free products. Anything with water needs a real preservative and training. Clean, sanitise with alcohol, and let everything dry.
Weigh your essential oils and stay within the ranges. And leave them out of baby products.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Start with water-free products
Water in it means a real preservative
Clean, sanitise, and let everything dry
Weigh essential oils; body 1 to 3%
No essential oils in baby products
